Archive item 2: Change Request CR-2024-014
Source format: change request

This change request seeks to revise the preventive maintenance schedule for the solar PV arrays located in the Port Harcourt cluster. Specifically, the bi-monthly cleaning cycle for the panel arrays at the Trans-Amadi and Rumuola substations will be adjusted to a monthly cycle during the dry season months of November through April. The wet season months of May through October will retain the existing bi-monthly cleaning schedule.

The change also includes the addition of a quarterly thermographic inspection of all combiner boxes and DC isolators within the cluster, which is not currently covered under the base contract scope. This inspection will be performed using an infrared camera and will include a written report with thermal images and recommendations for any corrective actions.

2. JUSTIFICATION

The adjustment to the cleaning cycle is driven by observed dust and particulate accumulation rates over the past nine months of operation. Data from the SCADA system indicate that average soiling losses on the Trans-Amadi array reached 6.8% during the peak dry season months of January and February 2024, compared to a baseline assumption of 3.5% used in the original energy yield model. Similar losses were recorded at Rumuola, though at slightly lower levels. The additional cleaning passes are expected to recover approximately 2.5–3.0% of the annual energy yield, which corresponds to an estimated 180–215 MWh per year across the two substations.

The thermographic inspection is justified on the basis of two separate incidents in April 2024 where hot spots were detected on DC isolators during manual checks. In both cases, the isolators had to be replaced under emergency call-out, incurring additional cost and downtime. Routine thermographic scanning is expected to identify such defects at an earlier stage, allowing for planned replacements during scheduled maintenance windows rather than reactive call-outs.

3. IMPACT ASSESSMENT

3.1 Cost Impact

The estimated additional cost for the revised cleaning schedule is NGN 2,850,000 per annum. This is based on the deployment of two additional cleaning crews during the dry season months, including labour, water supply, and equipment usage.

The thermographic inspection service is quoted at NGN 1,200,000 per inspection, to be performed four times per year. This brings the total annual additional cost to NGN 7,650,000.

3.2 Schedule Impact

No extension to the overall contract duration is required. The additional cleaning passes will be integrated into the existing maintenance calendar, with specific dates to be agreed at the monthly coordination meeting. The thermographic inspections will be scheduled to coincide with the quarterly preventive maintenance visits to avoid additional mobilisation costs.

3.3 Technical Impact

No modifications to the plant design, control systems, or safety procedures are required. The additional activities are within the existing competency of the site maintenance team and the approved subcontractor list.

Upon approval, the revised cleaning schedule will take effect from 1 August 2024, allowing for the first monthly cleaning pass to be completed before the onset of the next dry season. Reference: Change Request CR-2024-014 – Additional Cleaning Passes and Thermographic Inspections

Contract: O&M Services Agreement – Port Harcourt Cluster (Contract No. SV/PH/2022/OM/014)

Reporting Period: 1 August 2024 – 31 December 2024

Prepared by: Engr. Ibrahim Musa, Maintenance Manager, Port Harcourt Cluster

Date: 9 January 2025

Distribution: Adaobi Okafor (Contracts Manager), Engr. Chinedu Okafor (Head of Engineering), Mrs. Funke Adeyemi (Commercial Manager), Client Representative (SunVest Energy Services Nigeria Limited/Client)

1. PURPOSE

This report documents the implementation of approved Change Request CR-2024-014, covering the period from the effective date of 1 August 2024 through 31 December 2024. The report confirms completion of the additional cleaning passes and the first two thermographic inspections, records any deviations encountered, and provides the basis for the first invoice under the revised scope.

2. BACKGROUND

CR-2024-014 was approved on 10 July 2024. The change introduced two additional cleaning crews during the dry season months (November to April) and thermographic inspections of the PV arrays and inverter terminations. The approved contract value for the change is NGN 7,650,000 per annum, comprising NGN 2,850,000 for the additional cleaning crews and NGN 1,200,000 per inspection for four thermographic inspections per year. The schedule impact was nil; the additional activities were to be integrated into the existing maintenance calendar.

3. IMPLEMENTATION SUMMARY

3.1 Additional Cleaning Crews

The two additional cleaning crews were mobilised on 1 August 2024, ahead of the dry season. Each crew is composed of four operators, one supervisor, and one water tanker driver. The crews were sourced from the approved subcontractor list (SunVest approved subcontractors – Port Harcourt Cluster, Rev. 4). No new subcontractors were introduced.

Cleaning passes completed between 1 August 2024 and 31 December 2024:

- August 2024: 1 pass (wet season baseline cleaning of all arrays)
- September 2024: 1 pass (scheduled cleaning following heavy Harmattan dust ingress)
- October 2024: 1 pass (pre-dry season deep clean)
- November 2024: 2 passes (dry season commencement – increased frequency)
- December 2024: 2 passes (dry season continued)

Total passes completed: 7. This is consistent with the approved schedule of monthly cleaning during wet season and twice-monthly cleaning during dry season. The dry season frequency commenced on 1 November 2024 as agreed at the October coordination meeting.

Water usage for cleaning averaged 14,500 litres per pass. Water was sourced from the site borehole and supplemented by the Port Harcourt municipal supply when borehole output was low. No water quality issues were encountered that impacted cleaning effectiveness.

3.2 Thermographic Inspections

Two thermographic inspections were performed during the reporting period:

- Inspection 1: 12 September 2024 – performed by ThermalScan Nigeria Limited.
- Inspection 2: 3 December 2024 – performed by ThermalScan Nigeria Limited.

Both inspections covered the full PV array (12,480 modules) and all inverter terminations (48 inverters). Inspection reports were submitted to the site office within five working days of each inspection. Findings are summarised in Section 4 of this report.

3.3 Coordination

Monthly coordination meetings were held as scheduled (August, September, October, November, December). The revised cleaning schedule was integrated into the monthly maintenance calendar without conflict with preventive maintenance activities. No additional mobilisation was required for the thermographic inspections as they were aligned with the quarterly preventive maintenance visits.

1.4 The Contractor shall comply with all applicable Nigerian laws, regulations, and industry standards, including the Nigerian Electricity Regulatory Commission (NERC) grid codes and the Health, Safety and Environment (HSE) requirements of the Client.

2. TERM AND COMMENCEMENT

2.1 This Agreement shall commence on 15 January 2023 and shall continue in force for an initial period of twenty-four (24) months, unless terminated earlier in accordance with Clause 10.

2.2 The term may be renewed by mutual written agreement of the Parties for successive periods. Any renewal shall be subject to renegotiation of the Service Fees set out in Clause 4.

3. CONTRACTOR'S OBLIGATIONS

3.1 The Contractor shall perform the Works with all due skill, care, and diligence, using qualified personnel.

3.2 The Contractor shall assign a dedicated Site Manager who shall be the single point of contact for the Client. The Site Manager shall be available during working hours (Monday to Friday, 0800 to 1700 WAT) and shall be contactable by phone outside these hours for emergencies.

3.3 The Contractor shall maintain a response time of:
(a) Four (4) hours for critical failures (loss of generation or safety hazard);
(b) Twenty-four (24) hours for major failures (significant reduction in generation);
(c) Seventy-two (72) hours for minor failures.

3.4 The Contractor shall submit a monthly service report to the Client by the fifth (5th) day of the following month, detailing all activities performed, equipment status, and any recommendations.

3.5 The Contractor shall maintain records of all maintenance activities, including date, time, personnel, and parts used, and shall make such records available to the Client upon request.

4. SERVICE FEES AND PAYMENT

4.1 The Client shall pay the Contractor a fixed monthly service fee of NGN 2,850,000 (Two Million Eight Hundred and Fifty Thousand Naira), exclusive of VAT, for the performance of the Works (the "Service Fee").

4.2 The Service Fee shall be payable monthly in arrears, within thirty (30) days of receipt of a valid invoice and the monthly service report.

4.3 In addition to the Service Fee, the Client shall reimburse the Contractor for:
(a) The cost of consumables and minor spare parts (unit cost below NGN 150,000), with a monthly cap of NGN 400,000;
(b) Travel and accommodation costs incurred by the Contractor's personnel when attending to call-outs outside the Port Harcourt metropolitan area;
(c) Any costs associated with emergency call-outs requested by the Client outside normal working hours.

4.4 The Contractor may invoice for reimbursable costs under Clause 4.3 on a monthly basis. All invoices shall be in Naira and shall include a breakdown of costs.

4.5 Late payments shall attract interest at the rate of 2% per month, compounded, from the due date until the date of payment.

5. CLIENT'S OBLIGATIONS

5.1 The Client shall provide the Contractor with safe access to the site, including all necessary keys, passes, and permits.

5.2 The Client shall provide a designated point of contact for the Contractor and shall respond to the Contractor's requests for information or decisions within five (5) working days.

5.3 The Client shall ensure that the site is free from hazards that could endanger the Contractor's personnel and shall inform the Contractor of any known site-specific risks.

5.4 The Client shall be responsible for the security of the site and for any damage to the Contractor's equipment or personnel caused by third parties, except where such damage is caused by the negligence of the Contractor.

6. LIABILITY AND INSURANCE

Change Request CR-2024-014
documents.content:
This change request seeks to revise the preventive maintenance schedule for the solar PV arrays located in the Port Harcourt cluster. Specifically, the bi-monthly cleaning cycle for the panel arrays at the Trans-Amadi and Rumuola substations will be adjusted to a monthly cycle during the dry season months of November through April. The wet season months of May through October will retain the existing bi-monthly cleaning schedule.

The change also includes the addition of a quarterly thermographic inspection of all combiner boxes and DC isolators within the cluster, which is not currently covered under the base contract scope. This inspection will be performed using an infrared camera and will include a written report with thermal images and recommendations for any corrective actions.

2. JUSTIFICATION

The adjustment to the cleaning cycle is driven by observed dust and particulate accumulation rates over the past nine months of operation. Data from the SCADA system indicate that average soiling losses on the Trans-Amadi array reached 6.8% during the peak dry season months of January and February 2024, compared to a baseline assumption of 3.5% used in the original energy yield model. Similar losses were recorded at Rumuola, though at slightly lower levels. The additional cleaning passes are expected to recover approximately 2.5–3.0% of the annual energy yield, which corresponds to an estimated 180–215 MWh per year across the two substations.

The thermographic inspection is justified on the basis of two separate incidents in April 2024 where hot spots were detected on DC isolators during manual checks. In both cases, the isolators had to be replaced under emergency call-out, incurring additional cost and downtime. Routine thermographic scanning is expected to identify such defects at an earlier stage, allowing for planned replacements during scheduled maintenance windows rather than reactive call-outs.

3. IMPACT ASSESSMENT

3.1 Cost Impact

The estimated additional cost for the revised cleaning schedule is NGN 2,850,000 per annum. This is based on the deployment of two additional cleaning crews during the dry season months, including labour, water supply, and equipment usage.

The thermographic inspection service is quoted at NGN 1,200,000 per inspection, to be performed four times per year. This brings the total annual additional cost to NGN 7,650,000.

3.2 Schedule Impact

No extension to the overall contract duration is required. The additional cleaning passes will be integrated into the existing maintenance calendar, with specific dates to be agreed at the monthly coordination meeting. The thermographic inspections will be scheduled to coincide with the quarterly preventive maintenance visits to avoid additional mobilisation costs.

3.3 Technical Impact

No modifications to the plant design, control systems, or safety procedures are required. The additional activities are within the existing competency of the site maintenance team and the approved subcontractor list.

Upon approval, the revised cleaning schedule will take effect from 1 August 2024, allowing for the first monthly cleaning pass to be completed before the onset of the next dry season. IMPLEMENTATION COMPLETION REPORT – CR-2024-014

Reference: Change Request CR-2024-014 – Additional Cleaning Passes and Thermographic Inspections

Contract: O&M Services Agreement – Port Harcourt Cluster (Contract No. SV/PH/2022/OM/014)

Reporting Period: 1 August 2024 – 31 December 2024

Prepared by: Engr. Ibrahim Musa, Maintenance Manager, Port Harcourt Cluster

Date: 9 January 2025

Distribution: Adaobi Okafor (Contracts Manager), Engr. Chinedu Okafor (Head of Engineering), Mrs. Funke Adeyemi (Commercial Manager), Client Representative (SunVest Energy Services Nigeria Limited/Client)

1. PURPOSE

This report documents the implementation of approved Change Request CR-2024-014, covering the period from the effective date of 1 August 2024 through 31 December 2024. The report confirms completion of the additional cleaning passes and the first two thermographic inspections, records any deviations encountered, and provides the basis for the first invoice under the revised scope.

2. BACKGROUND

CR-2024-014 was approved on 10 July 2024. The change introduced two additional cleaning crews during the dry season months (November to April) and thermographic inspections of the PV arrays and inverter terminations. The approved contract value for the change is NGN 7,650,000 per annum, comprising NGN 2,850,000 for the additional cleaning crews and NGN 1,200,000 per inspection for four thermographic inspections per year. The schedule impact was nil; the additional activities were to be integrated into the existing maintenance calendar.

3. IMPLEMENTATION SUMMARY

3.1 Additional Cleaning Crews

The two additional cleaning crews were mobilised on 1 August 2024, ahead of the dry season. Each crew is composed of four operators, one supervisor, and one water tanker driver. The crews were sourced from the approved subcontractor list (SunVest approved subcontractors – Port Harcourt Cluster, Rev. 4). No new subcontractors were introduced.

Cleaning passes completed between 1 August 2024 and 31 December 2024:

- August 2024: 1 pass (wet season baseline cleaning of all arrays)
- September 2024: 1 pass (scheduled cleaning following heavy Harmattan dust ingress)
- October 2024: 1 pass (pre-dry season deep clean)
- November 2024: 2 passes (dry season commencement – increased frequency)
- December 2024: 2 passes (dry season continued)

Total passes completed: 7. This is consistent with the approved schedule of monthly cleaning during wet season and twice-monthly cleaning during dry season. The dry season frequency commenced on 1 November 2024 as agreed at the October coordination meeting.

Water usage for cleaning averaged 14,500 litres per pass. Water was sourced from the site borehole and supplemented by the Port Harcourt municipal supply when borehole output was low. No water quality issues were encountered that impacted cleaning effectiveness.

3.2 Thermographic Inspections

Two thermographic inspections were performed during the reporting period:

- Inspection 1: 12 September 2024 – performed by ThermalScan Nigeria Limited.
- Inspection 2: 3 December 2024 – performed by ThermalScan Nigeria Limited.

Both inspections covered the full PV array (12,480 modules) and all inverter terminations (48 inverters). Inspection reports were submitted to the site office within five working days of each inspection. Findings are summarised in Section 4 of this report.

3.3 Coordination

Monthly coordination meetings were held as scheduled (August, September, October, November, December). The revised cleaning schedule was integrated into the monthly maintenance calendar without conflict with preventive maintenance activities. No additional mobilisation was required for the thermographic inspections as they were aligned with the quarterly preventive maintenance visits.
